findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "download_video" stacks urgency/override words (important, always). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Download a video or audio file from any supported platform: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram (public reels, feed video, photo posts, and carousels), SoundCloud, Vimeo…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: download_video, get_video_info · Private data: download_video · Public sink: get_video_info · Destructive: download_video.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: download_video, get_video_info · Private data: download_video · Public sink: get_video_info · Destructive: download_video

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "download_video" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
